title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

errors: No mathematical error is visible. Lemma 2 is stated without proof. Its local-to-global direction for ≪ and ∥ silently uses Prop. 4 (gluing of refinements) together with the requirement that the F_i cover F. The claim 'idem pour ... ≪ ...' for two refinements G, G' of F is plausible given that gluing, but it is not argued.

ideas.what: Locality of relations (≤, ∥, ≭, ≪) between subdivisions of a figure with respect to a cover by subfigures (Lemma 2), complementing the sheaf property of refinements
ideas.modern_name: Sheaf/stack-like descent for subdivisions of polyhedral/CW complexes; locality of order relations on subdivisions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in PL topology (subdivisions are determined locally, e.g. Rourke–Sanderson style arguments)

ideas.what: Programme of an axiomatic 'analysis situs' via primitive relations ≤, ≪, |∘| on a set of pieces, with 'lieux' (points) as ≪-minimal elements, opens and multi-opens, and set-theoretic models
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology / combinatorial (pointless) foundations of stratified spaces; close in spirit to o-minimal structures and face posets of regular CW complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme §5, 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 calls for tame topology but does not, to my knowledge, contain this specific axiomatics

ideas.what: Expressing the refinement relation ≪ through the face relation ≤ and the interior relation |∘|, requiring formal interiors X° = X \ ∂X with ∂X = X̃ \ {X} and an inclusion relation of interiors
ideas.modern_name: Definability of subdivision from face poset plus interior-incidence; open cells of a regular cell complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: No clear modern counterpart as an axiomatic statement

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets an explicit open problem in his relational axiomatics. In the 'most common' case the refinement relation ≪ should be expressible from ≤ and |∘|, but stating this needs a formal theory of interiors X° and inclusion of interiors, via a 'theory of segments'. This reduction of subdivision to face and interior-incidence data is, as far as I know, not carried out in the literature on tame topology or cell posets.
missed.quote: Voir ce que devient l'axiomatique ≤, ≪, |∘|, dans ce cas (le plus courant sûrement) où ≪ peut s'exprimer en termes de ≤, |∘|. Mais pour la formuler, nous aurons besoin de donner un sens, pour X ∈ M, à "X° = X \ ∂X"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a purely combinatorial/relational foundation for tame or stratified topology in which subdivision is a derived notion. It could be relevant to synthetic/combinatorial approaches to stratified spaces, exit-path categories, and formalization of PL topology.

deep.surprise_reason: The lemma itself is a routine locality statement. The interest lies in the glimpse of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic analysis situs programme, notably reducing ≪ to ≤ and |∘|. That programme is unfinished but is only sketched on this page.
transcription_corrections: The relation written '|||' in 'idem pour |||, ≤, ≪' is most likely the disjointness relation ∥ used elsewhere in these notes.
'G_{F_i}' in the lemma denotes the restriction G|F_i, as in the first line.
Line 1, crossed out: 'Tout ceci est récapitulatif, ne fait pas intervenir |∘|. ...'; the struck-out word before 'Lem 2' is uncertain ('Prop. 11' / 'Rapp.' are both doubtful readings).
